proposal.title: One-click class-wide reteach set from the most-missed concept
proposal.rationale: Teacher-day analytics already surface 'which concepts the class is missing' and per-student practice already regenerates from an individual student's gap (demo.hub: 'one click and the practice writes itself'), but there's no equivalent for the whole-class signal — the teacher can see the class-wide gap but has no single action to turn it into a lesson.
proposal.change: Add a 'Reteach this' action on the class-level missed-concept signal in the teacher analytics view that calls the existing generation pipeline (assignment_generation.py) to draft a short worked-example + practice set for the whole class around that concept, verified the same way generated assignments already are before the teacher sees it.

proposal.title: Let students revisit their own past understanding-check conversations
proposal.rationale: Every integrity-check turn is stored for audit and Weak Spots/Review already surfaces recurring error patterns, but the feature map shows no student-facing view of the understanding-check conversation itself — the one moment a student had to explain their own reasoning out loud is currently teacher/admin-only.
proposal.change: Add a read-only 'review the conversation' view for students on their own past submissions, reusing the stored integrity_check turn history, so they can revisit what they were asked and how they explained their steps as a self-study aid.

proposal.title: Show a per-student understanding-check trend over time, not just per-submission
proposal.rationale: The integrity check already emits a per-submission badge/verdict (api/models/integrity_check.py) and the teacher's per-student grades/practice-history page exists, but there's no longitudinal view of a single student's understanding-check outcomes across the term — a teacher currently has to judge each submission in isolation instead of spotting a pattern (e.g. a student who repeatedly can't explain their own steps).
proposal.change: Add a small trend strip (badge history over recent submissions) to the teacher's per-student grade/practice-history view, sourced from existing integrity_check records, so recurring struggle patterns are visible without opening each submission.

proposal.title: Let a teacher ask the grading AI a follow-up question on one problem before approving
proposal.rationale: Grading pre-fills the teacher's review page with a per-problem justification (grading_ai.py), but the review flow is one-directional — the teacher can only accept or hand-edit the grade, not interrogate the reasoning behind a specific score before approving it, which slows trust-building on borderline grades.
proposal.change: Add a lightweight 'ask about this grade' affordance on each problem in the grade-review page that lets the teacher send a follow-up question to the same grading context and see the AI's reasoning inline, before they approve or edit that problem's score.

proposal.title: Add a cross-assignment concept-mastery trend view to the teacher-day dashboard
proposal.rationale: PRODUCT_CONTEXT.md describes teacher-day analytics as surfacing "which concepts the class is missing" but ties this to practice-activity per assignment; there's no described view of how a concept's mastery trends across the term, so a teacher can't tell whether a reteach actually worked or a concept is decaying again weeks later.
proposal.change: Add a per-concept trend line/sparkline to the teacher-day analytics view that plots class mastery on that concept across assignments over the term, so a reteach's effect is visible over time instead of only in the current assignment's snapshot.

proposal.title: Let a teacher turn a flagged weak-concept signal directly into a targeted reteach set for just the affected students
proposal.rationale: PRODUCT_CONTEXT.md says teacher-day gives "a path from a struggle signal to a reteach/practice set," and generation already re-derives/checks answers before the teacher sees them, but the described flow still requires the teacher to manually go generate a set from a worksheet/topic — there's no one-click bridge from the specific flagged concept + affected-student list to an assigned practice set for only those students.
proposal.change: On the teacher-day to-do list, add a "Reteach this" action next to a flagged weak concept that pre-fills the question-bank generator with that concept and auto-assigns the resulting practice set to only the students who showed the gap.

proposal.title: Add the admin dashboard's dev origin to the API's CORS allowlist
proposal.rationale: Every admin surface's console_errors in findings.json shows the same failure: 'Access to fetch ... from origin http://localhost:5173 has been blocked by CORS policy' plus 'net::ERR_FAILED', and every one of the 5 admin screenshots renders only the 'No response from the backend' / 'Couldn't load this view' error state, not the actual dashboard. Root cause confirmed in code: api/config.py:47-53 defines the default cors_origins list as localhost:8081, localhost:3000, and the prod domains, but omits localhost:5173 — the dashboard's default Vite dev port, which is documented as such in tests/harness/improver/surfaces.py:5 ('admin → dashboard/src/App.tsx (Vite/React, default :5173)').
proposal.change: In api/config.py, add "http://localhost:5173" to the default `cors_origins` list (alongside the existing localhost:8081 / localhost:3000 entries) so the dashboard's local dev server is allowed to call the API without a CORS block.

proposal.title: Fix the stale /present/* route catalog for the sales demo's deep-dive stories
proposal.rationale: demo.present, demo.present_integrity, demo.present_grading, demo.present_generation, and demo.present_teacher_day all report the exact same 4 hits and, on inspection, the same pixel-identical screenshot as demo.hub (verified: demo.present_grading.png == demo.hub.png). Root cause: tests/harness/improver/surfaces.py:92-96 lists these surfaces at '/present', '/present/integrity', '/present/grading', '/present/generation', '/present/teacher-day', but demo/src/App.tsx's actual router only defines '/integrity', '/grading', '/generation', '/teacher-day' (no '/present' prefix, and no standalone '/present' overview route at all) — every one of those catalog URLs 404s and the catch-all route silently redirects back to the hub. The improve-loop has effectively been re-scanning the hub 5 extra times and has never actually seen the 4 real story pages.
proposal.change: Update the surface catalog in tests/harness/improver/surfaces.py to the router's real paths ('/integrity', '/grading', '/generation', '/teacher-day') and drop the non-existent standalone '/present' overview entry (or add a real '/present' route in demo/src/App.tsx if an overview page distinct from the hub is actually wanted) so future scans cover the real story pages instead of quintuple-counting the hub.

proposal.title: Close the self-study loop: one-click practice + resolved tracking on Weak Spots
proposal.rationale: api/routes/weak_spots.py returns a flat, never-resolved list of flagged problems ('dedupe by problem text ... keep the most recent diagnosis summary') with no field or logic marking a weak spot resolved after the student later gets a similar problem right. Per PRODUCT_CONTEXT.md, Practice today generates from 'a seed or an assignment' — there's no route from a specific Review/Weak-Spots item straight into a practice set targeting exactly that gap for independent (non-school) students, even though the equivalent teacher-side loop (struggle signal -> reteach set) already ships (practice-struggle-panel.tsx). Self-study students can see they're weak on something but have no one-click way to drill it, and never see it marked as improved.
proposal.change: Add a 'Practice this' action on each Weak Spots item that seeds Practice generation from that specific problem, and track resolution (e.g. mark the weak-spot row resolved once the student answers a similar auto-generated problem correctly) so Review shows progress, not just an ever-growing list of past misses.

proposal.title: Generate a whole-class reteach mini-lesson from a missing-concept signal
proposal.rationale: The landing page and PRODUCT_CONTEXT.md describe teacher-day analytics surfacing 'which concepts the class is missing' with a one-click path to a practice set for individual students ('See the gap, fix it in one click'). There's no equivalent one-click artifact for reteaching the whole class the missing concept itself (a short worked-example explainer) before the next practice set — today the loop jumps straight from 'concept gap detected' to 'assign more practice' with nothing to reteach the concept in between.
proposal.change: Add a 'Generate reteach' action next to a flagged class-wide concept gap in the teacher analytics view that produces a short AI-drafted mini-lesson (worked example + common-mistake callout) for the teacher to review and share before assigning the follow-up practice set — reusing the existing generation/verification pipeline (assignment_generation.py) rather than a new one.

proposal.title: Show students a recap of what tripped them up in their understanding check
proposal.rationale: The integrity understanding-check conversation and its reasoning are currently surfaced to the teacher only ('you see the grade, the flag, the full conversation... and you decide' per PRODUCT_CONTEXT.md and the landing copy). The student side of the loop ends at the chat itself, with no learning artifact handed back — the exact population (a student who got the right answer without understanding) is the one most likely to benefit from a short 'here's the concept you couldn't quite explain' recap immediately after.
proposal.change: After an understanding-check conversation completes, show the student a short recap card (the concept the check probed and a one-line explanation) on their homework detail screen, generated from the same per-problem reasoning already produced by integrity_ai.py.

proposal.title: Add a one-click 'Generate reteach set' button from a flagged weak concept
proposal.rationale: PRODUCT_CONTEXT.md describes teacher-day analytics surfacing "which concepts the class is missing" and promises "a path from a struggle signal to a reteach/practice set," but the generation engine (assignment_generation.py / question_bank_generation.py) starts from a manually chosen worksheet or topic — the two capabilities exist but aren't wired together, so the teacher has to retype the weak concept by hand.
proposal.change: On the teacher-day/practice-activity analytics view, add a button on each flagged weak-concept row that opens the existing generation flow pre-scoped to that concept and grade level, reusing the already-verified generation pipeline rather than building new grading/generation logic.

proposal.title: Show the student a short recap after their integrity understanding-check
proposal.rationale: PRODUCT_CONTEXT.md notes the integrity check "emits per-problem badges/confidence/reasoning" that feed the teacher's review, but describes no equivalent moment on the student side (Learn/Practice/Review) that tells the student what the conversation revealed about their own understanding — the loop closes for the teacher but not for the student who just did the work.
proposal.change: After the one-on-one integrity conversation ends, show the student a brief recap ("what you explained well / what to revisit") that links directly into an existing Practice set for the flagged concept, reusing current practice generation with no new grading logic.

proposal.title: One-click reteach packet generated from the class's most-missed concept
proposal.rationale: PRODUCT_CONTEXT.md describes teacher-day analytics that already surface 'which concepts the class is missing' and a separate generation engine that turns a worksheet/topic into a verified problem set, but no capability connects the two — a teacher who sees a slipping concept still has to manually start a new generation job and pick the topic themselves.
proposal.change: Add a button on the teacher-day / analytics view, next to a flagged 'concept the class is missing,' that pre-fills the existing question-bank generation flow with that concept as the topic, so the teacher goes from 'here's what they're missing' to a reviewable practice set in one click instead of two disconnected steps.

proposal.title: Add a visible level-one heading to each admin ops page
proposal.rationale: axe 'page-has-heading-one' fires on all 4 sales/ops admin pages (Leads, Schools, Harness runs, LLM calls); admin.quality doesn't hit this rule, showing the pattern isn't universal in the admin app and these 4 specifically lost/never got their h1.
proposal.change: Add an <h1> with the page title (e.g. 'Leads', 'Schools', 'Harness runs', 'LLM calls') at the top of each of these 4 admin route components, matching the pattern already present on the Quality page.

proposal.title: Let a student retake/reupload a photo in-app when extraction marks it skipped_unreadable
proposal.rationale: PRODUCT_CONTEXT.md notes a submission the integrity check can't read is marked 'skipped_unreadable' rather than penalized — but the feature map has no described recovery path for the student once that happens, leaving the submission stuck ungraded with no student-facing next step.
proposal.change: When a submission comes back skipped_unreadable (or extraction confidence is low), surface an in-app prompt on the student's homework-detail screen to retake/reupload the photo before the teacher's review window, closing the loop instead of leaving it silently blocked.

proposal.title: Add a main landmark and fix low-contrast text in the sales demo shell
proposal.rationale: All 6 demo/present routes share identical axe hits from the same shell layout: color-contrast (13 elements each), missing 'landmark-one-main' (all content sits outside a <main>), an <aside> nested inside another landmark instead of top-level, and 38 elements not contained by any landmark region. Since every present-mode page (integrity, grading, generation, teacher-day) reuses one shell component, this is one fix, not four.
proposal.change: In the demo app's shared shell/layout component, wrap the page body in a single <main>, move the sidebar <aside> to be a top-level landmark sibling (not nested inside another landmark), and darken the muted caption/label text color to meet WCAG AA contrast.

proposal.title: Let students ask a follow-up chat about any graded problem, not just the sampled integrity ones
proposal.rationale: PRODUCT_CONTEXT.md notes the integrity understanding-check only samples ~3 primary problems per submission for a one-on-one conversation; every other graded problem gets a receipt/justification but no way for the student to probe it further. Extending the same guided-conversation pattern to any graded problem (not just the sampled ones) would deepen the grade -> understand step of the core loop for the whole submission.
proposal.change: Add an 'Ask why' action on each graded problem in the student's submission view that opens a short guided chat (reusing the existing tutoring/integrity conversation pattern) grounded in that problem's grading receipt — guiding the student to see their mistake rather than stating the correct answer.

proposal.title: Surface a multi-assignment understanding trend per student, not just the latest snapshot
proposal.rationale: PRODUCT_CONTEXT.md describes teacher-day as ranking 'the handful of students who need them first' from current data, and weak-spots as surfacing 'recurring error patterns' — both read as point-in-time or pattern-based, not a trend across assignments. A student whose integrity/grade confidence is quietly declining over 3-4 assignments could look fine on any single day's to-do list.
proposal.change: Add a small trend indicator (e.g. a sparkline or ↑/↓ badge) next to each student on the teacher-day to-do list showing their grade/understanding trajectory over their last several assignments, so a slow decline surfaces even when the latest submission alone wouldn't rank them near the top.

proposal.title: Fix the demo surface catalog's dead /present/* URLs
proposal.rationale: demo.present, demo.present_integrity, demo.present_grading, demo.present_generation, and demo.present_teacher_day all report identical hit counts (13 contrast elements, 38 un-landmarked elements) — identical to demo.hub. That's because they render the same page: demo/src/App.tsx only registers routes at /integrity, /grading, /generation, /teacher-day (no /present prefix, and demo/src/lib/present-stories.ts:16-19 confirms there's no /present index route either); any /present/* URL falls through the catch-all Navigate-to-'/' route. The improver has been re-crawling the hub five times under different surface keys instead of ever rendering the four actual story pages.
proposal.change: Update the demo surface catalog (tests/harness/improver/surfaces.py) to point at the real paths — /integrity, /grading, /generation, /teacher-day — and drop the nonexistent /present overview entry, so future crawls actually evaluate the story pages instead of silently re-scoring the redirect target.

proposal.title: One-click concept-targeted reteach set from the teacher-day struggle signal
proposal.rationale: PRODUCT_CONTEXT.md describes the teacher-day loop as going 'from a struggle signal to a reteach/practice set,' and teacher-day analytics already surface which concepts the class is missing — but closing that loop today appears to require the teacher to manually open Generation and rebuild a set from scratch rather than acting directly on the flagged concept.
proposal.change: Add a 'Reteach this' action on a missing-concept analytics card that pre-fills Generation with that exact concept and pre-selects only the students who missed it, so the teacher goes from signal to an assignable set in one click.

proposal.title: Auto-draft a whole-class reteach mini-lesson when a misconception recurs
proposal.rationale: PRODUCT_CONTEXT.md describes teacher-day analytics surfacing "which concepts the class is missing" and a path to a practice set, but the generation engine (independently-verified answers, teacher-approved before it's trusted) is only ever pointed at a worksheet/topic today, not auto-triggered by a detected class-wide misconception signal from grading/integrity analytics.
proposal.change: When teacher-day analytics detects a concept missed by a threshold share of the class (e.g. >30%), surface a one-click "Draft a reteach mini-lesson" action next to that concept that runs the existing verified-generation pipeline against the specific missed concept and drops the draft into the teacher's review queue, same approve-before-publish pattern as assignment generation.

proposal.title: Add an opt-in parent digest summarizing understanding-check trends
proposal.rationale: The physics subject page's own FAQ asks "Can my parents see what I'm doing?" (web.public.subjects_physics screenshot), implying parent visibility is already a question the product invites but the feature map in PRODUCT_CONTEXT.md has no parent-facing surface — only student/teacher/admin roles exist today.
proposal.change: Add an opt-in weekly email digest for a student's parent/guardian, summarizing integrity-check verdicts and grade trends over the week (reusing existing integrity/grading data, no new grading logic) — read-only, no messaging or gradebook export, so it stays inside the AI loop rather than becoming an LMS feature.

proposal.title: Flag when a physics/chemistry miss traces back to a math prerequisite gap
proposal.rationale: PRODUCT_CONTEXT.md notes math is the mature subject while physics/chemistry are partial, and weak-spots/review already tracks recurring error patterns per subject in isolation — there's no cross-subject linkage today, even though a student's physics error (e.g. a botched free-body-diagram algebra step) is often really a math weak spot.
proposal.change: When weak-spots analysis on a physics/chemistry submission detects an error in an underlying algebra/arithmetic step (already extracted by the grading/integrity pipeline), tag it against the student's math weak-spots list instead of only the physics/chemistry one, so the teacher sees "this is a math gap showing up in physics" rather than two disconnected signals.

proposal.title: Add a guided tutor follow-up for problems marked wrong, not just suspiciously-correct ones
proposal.rationale: PRODUCT_CONTEXT.md says the integrity conversation runs 'before a correct answer is cleared' (api/core/integrity_ai.py) — it only engages the student when their answer looks right. A problem graded wrong or partial today only gets a written grade + justification with no conversational follow-up, so the 'understand' step of the homework -> grade -> understand -> reteach loop is skipped exactly where a struggling student needs it most.
proposal.change: On the student's grade view, add a one-tap 'Help me understand this' action on any problem marked wrong/partial that launches the existing Learn step-decomposition/tutor engine scoped to that specific missed problem (reusing tutor.py, not building a new tutoring path).

proposal.title: Pre-suggest generation topics from a section's weak-spot signals
proposal.rationale: PRODUCT_CONTEXT.md's feature map lists Generation (assignment_generation.py, question_bank_generation.py) as taking 'a worksheet (or a topic)' as input, and Weak spots (weak_spots.py, practice_activity) as a separate signal surfaced only in teacher-day analytics — there's no stated link where a class's actual weak-spot data feeds into what the generator proposes to build next.
proposal.change: In the 'Generate more questions' flow (seen in web.public.landing.png's product screenshot), pre-populate the topic/focus field with the section's current top weak-spot concepts pulled from practice_activity analytics, so generation targets what students are actually missing instead of requiring the teacher to pick a chapter from scratch.

proposal.title: Add a concept-mastery heatmap across a teacher's sections, not just per-section
proposal.rationale: The feature map states grade review and concept analytics exist 'per section and per student,' but a teacher running multiple sections of the same course has no described way to see a concept failing across ALL of their sections — a curriculum-level signal distinct from a single class's dip.
proposal.change: Add a rollup view (available from the teacher's course page) that aggregates concept-miss rates across every section of that course, so a concept weak everywhere stands out from one that's isolated to a single class.

proposal.title: Surface a per-student trend of recurring integrity/understanding-check flags
proposal.rationale: The integrity check emits a per-submission badge/verdict, and Weak Spots rolls up recurring *error patterns*, but PRODUCT_CONTEXT.md describes no rollup of recurring *understanding-check* flags over time — a teacher can't currently tell a one-off shaky explanation from a student who's flagged low-understanding on 3 of their last 4 submissions.
proposal.change: On the student's grade-review page, add a small trend indicator summarizing their integrity-check verdicts over recent assignments (e.g. flagged 3 of last 4), separate from the existing error-pattern-based Weak Spots.

proposal.title: Add a page-level h1 to admin dashboard pages
proposal.rationale: axe 'page-has-heading-one' fires on Leads, Schools, Harness runs, and LLM calls admin pages; admin.quality (same shell) does not, suggesting most admin pages already have a pattern for this except these four.
proposal.change: Add a visible <h1> page title (matching the sidebar nav label, e.g. 'Leads', 'Schools') to the top of each of these four admin dashboard views, consistent with how Quality already does it.

proposal.title: Resurface weak spots on a spaced-repetition schedule instead of only on-demand
proposal.rationale: PRODUCT_CONTEXT's Weak spots/Review capability lets a student 'study what you actually keep getting wrong,' but as described it's a static list the student must choose to open — nothing proactively resurfaces a past weak spot once it's likely to be forgotten.
proposal.change: Add a lightweight scheduler that re-queues a resolved-but-recent weak spot back into the student's Practice queue after a spaced interval (e.g. 3/7/14 days), reusing the existing weak_spots and practice infrastructure.

proposal.title: Let students revisit their own past understanding-check conversations
proposal.rationale: PRODUCT_CONTEXT.md §3 confirms every integrity turn "is stored for audit," but §4's student feature list has no surface for a student to reopen that transcript — it's currently teacher/admin-only audit data. Turning an existing audit artifact into a self-study review ("see how I explained this last time before I try a similar problem") is a small, low-risk addition that stays inside the homework→grade→understand loop and doesn't touch grading, integrity scoring, or any AI call.
proposal.change: On the student History/assignment-detail view, add a read-only "review my explanation" link for submissions that had an integrity check, showing the stored conversation transcript from api/models/integrity_check.py records.

proposal.title: Give students a longitudinal concept-mastery view, not just a static weak-spots list
proposal.rationale: PRODUCT_CONTEXT.md §3 describes Weak Spots/Review as surfacing "a student's recurring error patterns to review" — a present-tense snapshot. The feature map (§4) lists Home, Learn, Practice, Mock-test, Review, History for the student surface, but nothing that shows a student their mastery of a concept improving (or not) across assignments/practice/mock-tests over time. This is a genuine gap inside the existing "understand" step of the AI loop (not a new capability — it reuses grading + weak-spot data already collected) and is squarely student-facing self-study value, not an LMS feature.
proposal.change: Add a per-concept trend view (e.g. a simple sparkline/heat-row per topic) to the student Review/History surface, built from existing grade and weak-spot records grouped by concept over time, so a student can see "I used to miss this, now I don't" instead of only a current-state list.

proposal.title: Stop claiming 'full' physics/chemistry curriculum coverage on the subject pages
proposal.rationale: The /subjects/physics screenshot reads "Covers the full physics curriculum from conceptual physics through AP Physics C: mechanics, electricity, magnetism, and modern physics" and /subjects/chemistry reads "Covers the full chemistry curriculum from intro chem through AP Chemistry and organic" — both promise complete, math-equivalent coverage. PRODUCT_CONTEXT.md is explicit and owner-confirmed that "math is the full, mature subject; physics and chemistry are partial... engine depth beyond math is not complete," and directs ideate to "not assume they are on par with math." Districts (the actual buyer, per the product's own positioning) evaluate this copy directly, so overclaiming here creates a credibility gap the first time a pilot teacher hits the edge of physics/chemistry depth.
proposal.change: Soften the hero claim and the "Everything you wish your AI tool did" checklist on both subject pages to describe current depth honestly (e.g. "growing coverage of...") instead of "full curriculum," or hold the strongest completeness claims for math only.

proposal.title: Let a student flag an AI grade for teacher re-review
proposal.rationale: Product context states the teacher approves every AI grade before it posts, but there's no described path for a student who disagrees with a posted grade to raise it back to the teacher's queue — today the only lever is the teacher's own review pass.
proposal.change: Add a lightweight 'flag this grade' action on the student's graded-homework view that drops the submission back into the teacher's grade-review queue with the student's note attached, instead of requiring the teacher to notice on their own.

proposal.title: Add a class-wide misconception rollup after each assignment grades
proposal.rationale: Teacher-day analytics are described as per-student ('who needs you first') and per-concept over time, but nothing surfaces the single most common wrong step *within one assignment* right after grading finishes — the moment a teacher most wants a one-glance 'here's what tripped up the class' before opening individual submissions.
proposal.change: After a batch grading run completes, generate a short rollup (top 2-3 shared error patterns across the class for that assignment, with example submissions) shown at the top of the assignment's grade-review page.

proposal.title: Show a per-student score/concept trend line inline in the teacher's grade review
proposal.rationale: Teacher-day already surfaces 'which students are slipping' at the class level (practice_activity analytics), but the grade review page for an individual student's submission is a single-assignment snapshot — there's no quick way for a teacher to see whether this student's performance on this concept is a one-off miss or part of a multi-week decline while they're sitting in the review flow.
proposal.change: Add a small sparkline/trend strip to the per-student grade review view showing their last 5-6 assignment scores and most-missed concepts, sourced from existing practice_activity/submission grade history — no new data collection needed.

proposal.title: Fix CORS config so the admin dashboard can reach the API
proposal.rationale: Every admin surface (Leads, Schools, Quality, Harness runs, LLM calls) logs the identical console error: 'Access to fetch at http://localhost:8000/v1/admin/... from origin http://localhost:5173 has been blocked by CORS policy: Response to preflight request doesn't pass access control check: No Access-Control-Allow-Origin header'. The admin.leads screenshot confirms the visible effect: the whole view renders 'Couldn't load this view. Can't reach our servers right now.' with an 'API UNREACHABLE' badge in the sidebar and a top banner blaming the backend/Railway status, when the real cause is a missing Access-Control-Allow-Origin response header for the dashboard's origin.
proposal.change: Add the dashboard's origin (localhost:5173 in dev, and its deployed admin host in prod) to the API's CORS allow-list so preflight OPTIONS requests to /v1/admin/* succeed; verify with the network tab that Access-Control-Allow-Origin is present on both the preflight and the actual response.

proposal.title: Let a teacher flag an AI grade or generated question as wrong, straight into the quality pipeline
proposal.rationale: The product already treats AI quality as first-class internally (LLM call logging, harness runs, a golden set, and a grading-quality dashboard all live under admin/quality per PRODUCT_CONTEXT.md), but there's no teacher-facing capability listed in the feature map for a teacher to flag a specific bad grade justification or a bad generated question at the point they see it during grade review or question-bank review. Today that signal, if it exists at all, has to travel informally instead of into the golden set.
proposal.change: Add a lightweight 'flag as wrong' action on the grade-review and question-bank-review surfaces that captures the submission/question id + teacher's one-line reason and writes it into the existing quality/golden-set review queue the admin dashboard already surfaces — closing the loop from 'teacher caught an AI mistake' to 'it shows up in Quality for someone to fix', without any new grading/auto-flag behavior.

proposal.title: Investigate failing `integrity_extract` LLM calls

proposal.rationale: PRODUCT_CONTEXT.md describes teacher-day as surfacing 'which concepts the class is missing' with 'a path from a struggle signal to a reteach/practice set,' and Practice already generates unlimited similar problems from a seed/assignment — but the feature map has no capability that turns a detected weak-concept signal directly into a ready-to-assign mini-reteach (a short worked example plus a fresh practice set targeting that concept), only generic per-assignment practice. This would close the reteach step of the loop the same way Generation already closes the assignment step.
proposal.change: On the teacher-day analytics view, add a 'Reteach this' action next to the top missed concept that calls the existing generation pipeline (assignment_generation.py/question_bank_generation.py) with that concept as the seed, producing one short worked example plus a small practice set the teacher can review and assign in one click.

proposal.title: Fix the improver's demo-story URLs so it actually checks the 4 story pages
proposal.rationale: The 5 'demo.present*' screenshots are pixel-identical to demo.hub and share its exact hit set (13 contrast elements, 'aside not top-level', 'main landmark', 38-element region violation) — they never actually reached a distinct story page. Confirmed in code: tests/harness/improver/surfaces.py:92-96 catalogs the paths as `/present`, `/present/integrity`, `/present/grading`, `/present/generation`, `/present/teacher-day`, but demo/src/App.tsx defines the real routes as `/`, `/integrity`, `/grading`, `/generation`, `/teacher-day` (no `/present` prefix, and no separate 'overview' route) with a catch-all `<Route path="*" element={<Navigate to="/" replace />} />`. Every one of the 5 stale URLs silently redirects to the front door, so the four flagship sales-demo story pages (integrity, grading, generation, teacher-day) have never actually been crawled or checked for console errors/a11y regressions.
proposal.change: Update tests/harness/improver/surfaces.py:92-96 to use the real demo routes (`/integrity`, `/grading`, `/generation`, `/teacher-day`), and drop the non-existent separate '/present' overview entry since '/' (already covered by demo.hub) is the only front-door route.

proposal.title: Fix CORS policy blocking every admin dashboard API call
proposal.rationale: Console errors on all 5 captured admin surfaces show the browser blocking preflight requests from origin http://localhost:5173 to http://localhost:8000/v1/admin/* with 'No Access-Control-Allow-Origin header'. Screenshots confirm the user-visible result: admin.leads and admin.quality both render a full-page 'Couldn't load this view / Can't reach our servers right now' error banner plus a persistent 'API UNREACHABLE' sidebar badge — the entire admin app is non-functional, not a cosmetic issue.
proposal.change: Add the admin dashboard's origin(s) to the API's CORS allow-list (the FastAPI CORSMiddleware config in the api service) so admin.* fetches to /v1/admin/* succeed instead of failing preflight.

proposal.title: Let a teacher turn a 'class is missing this concept' signal directly into a targeted reteach set
proposal.rationale: PRODUCT_CONTEXT.md describes teacher-day analytics as surfacing 'which concepts the class is missing' and generation as turning a worksheet/topic a teacher supplies into a verified problem set — but the two are disconnected: today the teacher has to notice the gap, then manually start a new generation flow from scratch. There's no one-click path from the analytics signal to a ready-to-assign remediation set scoped to just the students who missed that concept.
proposal.change: On the teacher-day 'concepts the class is missing' view, add a per-concept 'Reteach this' action that pre-seeds the existing generation flow with that concept and pre-selects the students who got it wrong, so the teacher lands on a review-ready set instead of a blank generation form.

proposal.title: Let a student flag 'I couldn't solve this' instead of submitting a guess
proposal.rationale: PRODUCT_CONTEXT.md frames the student app as 'the input surface that feeds the teacher's loop' and grading/integrity as reading whatever photo comes in — but a student who's simply stuck has no way to say so; they either submit blank work or a guess, which the grader and integrity check then have to interpret as a wrong/unclear answer rather than a clear 'I need help here' signal.
proposal.change: Add an optional 'I'm stuck on this one' flag per problem at homework-submission time (alongside the photo), and surface it to the teacher's grade review and weak-spots analytics as a distinct signal from a wrong answer, so struggle is reported directly instead of inferred from grading.

proposal.title: Let a student ask the AI why they lost points, after grades are released
proposal.rationale: PRODUCT_CONTEXT.md describes grading as producing 'a per-problem grade' with a written justification ('receipt') and a separate pre-answer integrity conversation, but no post-release conversation for a student to follow up on a specific grade — grading is currently a one-way explanation, not a dialogue.
proposal.change: After a teacher publishes grades, add a short guided follow-up chat scoped to one problem's existing grade justification ('why did I lose points here / what should I do differently'), reusing the tutoring-guides-not-answers constraint already used in Learn mode.

proposal.title: Generate a class-wide reteach mini-lesson from a missed-concept signal
proposal.rationale: PRODUCT_CONTEXT.md describes teacher-day analytics surfacing 'which concepts the class is missing' with 'a path from a struggle signal to a reteach/practice set' — but per the feature map, generation today only produces problem sets (assignment/question-bank generation), not an explainer. When a whole class misses the same concept, a teacher needs to re-teach it, not just assign more repetitions of it.
proposal.change: From the teacher-day 'concept the class is missing' signal, add a one-click action that generates a short worked-example mini-lesson (the misconception, one annotated worked example, then a link into a practice set on that concept) using the existing generation pipeline's answer-verification step, so it's trustworthy before the teacher shows it in class.

proposal.title: Add a 'Learn step-by-step' action to the Weak Spots / Review screens
proposal.rationale: On the homework-detail grade review, a missed problem already offers both 'Practice similar' and 'Learn step-by-step' (web/src/app/(app)/school/student/courses/[courseId]/homework/[assignmentId]/page.tsx:806-891), which starts a LEARN-mode session on that exact problem via startLearnQueue. But the standalone Weak Spots / Review screens that resurface those same recurring errors later (web/src/app/(app)/review/page.tsx:66-80, mobile WeakSpotsScreen.tsx:57-69) only wire the 'Practice similar' action — a student revisiting a weak spot days later has no direct path back into a guided tutor session for it, only more cold practice problems.
proposal.change: Add the same 'Learn step-by-step' CTA used on the homework-detail page to the Weak Spots / Review list items, wired to startLearnQueue with that problem's text/subject.

proposal.title: Show a real multi-assignment concept-mastery trend, not just an earlier-vs-recent arrow
proposal.rationale: Teacher-day is meant to surface 'which concepts the class is missing' over time (PRODUCT_CONTEXT.md), but the only trend signal today is a binary comparison: GET .../student-insights' _derive_trend (api/routes/teacher_practice_activity.py:412-437) splits a student's practice history into 'earlier' vs. 'recent' (last third) and renders a single up/down/flat arrow — there's no per-assignment or per-week time series a teacher can actually read a pattern from.
proposal.change: Extend the student-insights/practice-insights response with a dated, per-assignment (or per-week) series of first-try/mastery rate per concept, and render it as a small trend chart instead of the single arrow in student-insights-tab.tsx.

proposal.title: Let teachers share question-bank sets within their school
proposal.rationale: The question bank (api/models/question_bank.py) is per-teacher today, but institutional schools have multiple teachers per subject/department independently generating overlapping problem sets from similar source material.
proposal.change: Let a teacher publish a question-bank set as shared-with-school, and let department colleagues browse and import (not edit) it into their own bank, cutting duplicate generation effort.

proposal.title: Surface a per-student understanding trend across assignments
proposal.rationale: Integrity checks already store per-submission badges/confidence/reasoning (api/models/integrity_check.py), but the feature map shows only one-off per-submission verdicts surfaced to the teacher — there's no view of whether a given student's understanding is improving or slipping over time.
proposal.change: Add a simple sparkline/trend of integrity confidence across a student's recent assignments to the teacher's grade-review or student-detail view.

proposal.title: Add the admin dashboard's dev origin to the API's CORS allowlist
proposal.rationale: Every admin surface logs identical console errors: "Access to fetch at 'http://localhost:8000/v1/admin/...' from origin 'http://localhost:5173' has been blocked by CORS policy: ... No 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin' header". The admin.leads screenshot confirms the user-visible effect: a full-page "Couldn't load this view" / "API unreachable" error banner instead of any data. api/config.py:47-53 hardcodes `cors_origins` to `localhost:8081`, `localhost:3000`, and two production hosts — `localhost:5173` (the admin app's Vite dev port) is absent, so every fetch from the admin dashboard is blocked at the browser level regardless of backend correctness.
proposal.change: Add "http://localhost:5173" to the `cors_origins` default list in api/config.py:47-53 (or move admin origins to an env-driven setting if the admin app is also served from a non-localhost origin in staging/prod) so the five admin dashboard pages can load their data.

proposal.title: Underline inline text links instead of relying on color alone
proposal.rationale: axe's link-in-text-block rule fires on register (2), privacy (3), terms (4), and support (1). The register screenshot confirms it visually: "Terms of Service" and "Privacy Policy" in the signup disclaimer are only distinguishable from surrounding gray text by their green color, with no underline or weight change — a failure for color-blind users.
proposal.change: Add a default underline (or matching text-decoration on hover/focus plus a non-color affordance) to inline links inside body-text blocks — the signup disclaimer and the prose links on the privacy/terms/support pages — rather than color alone.

proposal.title: Let students answer the integrity understanding-check by voice, not just typed text
proposal.rationale: PRODUCT_CONTEXT.md describes the integrity check as a warm one-on-one conversation probing the student to explain their own steps (api/core/integrity_ai.py, integrity_pipeline.py), but the feature map shows no speech input anywhere in the loop. Typing a multi-sentence explanation of your own math steps is exactly the moment where younger or struggling students disengage or give up early, undermining the check's core value.
proposal.change: Add a speech-to-text input option in the understanding-check chat (mobile and web) so a student can speak their explanation instead of typing it, transcribed into the same conversation turn the integrity pipeline already stores and scores.

proposal.title: Auto-draft a short reteach explainer when teacher-day analytics flag a class-wide missed concept
proposal.rationale: PRODUCT_CONTEXT.md's teacher-day capability surfaces "which concepts the class is missing" and a path to a "reteach/practice set" — but that path is student-facing practice, not something the teacher can use to actually reteach. There's no verified, teacher-facing artifact (worked example + the misconception to name aloud) for the concept the class is stuck on, only more problems for students to redo.
proposal.change: When teacher-day analytics identifies a concept most of the class missed, generate a one-page reteach explainer (2-3 worked examples plus the common error pattern to call out) using the same generation + answer-verification pipeline as question-bank generation, surfaced next to the existing practice-set suggestion.

proposal.title: Sort the teacher's grade-review queue by AI confidence, lowest first
proposal.rationale: PRODUCT_CONTEXT.md notes AI quality/confidence is already tracked and surfaced to admins (LLM calls, Quality, golden set dashboards), and grading 'pre-fills' the teacher's review page for every submission — but the teacher-facing review flow itself isn't described as prioritized by how confident the grader was. Teachers reviewing a full class one-by-one waste time double-checking answers the AI already nailed.
proposal.change: In the per-section grade review list, surface the AI's existing per-problem confidence score and default-sort so the lowest-confidence (most likely to need a teacher correction) submissions appear first.

proposal.title: Fix demo /present/* deep links to render their specific story
proposal.rationale: Screenshots for /present, /present/integrity, /present/grading, /present/generation, and /present/teacher-day are all visually identical to the demo hub's full scroll page (two are byte-identical by hash; the rest are pixel-identical on inspection) — none of the 4 dedicated 'story' present-mode views (integrity, grading, generation, teacher-day) actually render when the route is loaded directly. Per the product context, these 4 stories are the entire point of the sales demo.
proposal.change: Fix the demo app's routing/state so navigating directly to /present/{integrity,grading,generation,teacher-day} enters that story's present mode on load, instead of falling back to the generic hub scroll page — likely the present-mode view relies on client-side navigation state that isn't set when the route is loaded cold (e.g. a fresh tab or a shared link).

proposal.title: Let teachers configure how many problems get an integrity/understanding check
proposal.rationale: Today the integrity pipeline always samples ~3 primary problems per submission for the understanding-check conversation; teachers running short-answer quizzes vs. long problem sets have no way to tune how much class time this costs versus how much scrutiny they want.
proposal.change: Add a per-assignment setting (alongside the existing optional per-assignment integrity check toggle) letting the teacher choose how many problems get sampled for the understanding-check, trading off conversation depth against student time.

proposal.title: Give students a self-facing view of their own understanding-check history
proposal.rationale: Weak Spots already surfaces recurring error patterns to students, but the integrity/understanding-check verdicts and badges are currently only shown to the teacher — students never see their own trend of 'explained it well' vs 'couldn't explain it,' which is exactly the metacognitive signal the product is designed to produce.
proposal.change: Add a student-facing history view (parallel to Weak Spots) showing their own past understanding-check badges/verdicts over time, so students can see their own explain-your-work trend improve.

proposal.title: Show teachers which problems in a submission were / weren't understanding-checked
proposal.rationale: PRODUCT_CONTEXT.md section 3 states the integrity pipeline samples 'up to ~3 primary problems' per submission for the understanding check, not every problem — but the feature map (section 4) shows no teacher-facing indicator of which specific problems were covered versus skipped. Given the stated principle that integrity 'raises scrutiny, never auto-flags' and the teacher is meant to see the full picture, a submission with 6 problems where only 3 were probed currently looks the same to the teacher as one fully checked.
proposal.change: On the grade-review page, badge each problem as 'understanding checked' or 'not sampled for check', and let the teacher manually trigger a check on an unsampled problem before approving the grade.

proposal.title: Turn independent students' weak-spot patterns into a self-directed reteach plan
proposal.rationale: PRODUCT_CONTEXT.md section 3 describes Weak spots/Review (`api/routes/weak_spots.py`) as surfacing 'a student's recurring error patterns to review' for self-directed use, in contrast to the school teacher flow which has a stated one-click path 'from a struggle signal to a reteach/practice set' (section 3, Teacher-day). No equivalent generation step is described for independent students — they get the pattern surfaced but not a generated remediation plan, unlike the school-side flow.
proposal.change: Add a 'Fix this' action on the independent student's Weak Spots screen that generates a short Learn-mode mini-lesson + targeted practice set for that specific recurring error pattern, mirroring the teacher's one-click reteach flow.

proposal.title: Generate a ready-to-project reteach mini-lesson for a section's top missed concept
proposal.rationale: PRODUCT_CONTEXT.md describes teacher-day as surfacing 'which concepts the class is missing' with 'a path from a struggle signal to a reteach/practice set,' but the generation pipeline (assignment_generation.py, question_bank_generation.py) only produces problem sets — there's no generated explanatory content, so the teacher still has to build the actual reteach explanation from scratch.
proposal.change: Add a 'Generate reteach' action on the class concept-miss signal that calls generation to produce a short worked-example walkthrough (2-3 problems with step-by-step explanation, reusing step_decomposition.py's teachable-step logic) for the most-missed concept, answer-verified like existing generation, ready for the teacher to project in class.
